thread:
Jon: Heads-up — weird routing spike on canary. Dashboard shows canary got ~100% of traffic for ~2m around 16:10 UTC even though rollout set to 5/95.
Maria: which service/route?
Jon: /services/route-inference api-prod. Canary id canary-2026-03-20. Affected regions: mostly us-west1.
Kevin: Did you check header-based routing? X-Canary or X-User-Segment?
Jon: When X-Canary=1 present it's fine. When absent we expect hashing on cookie `rw-session` -> bucket. But logs show fallback to client_ip hash and chosen_bucket = 0 -> canary.
Ashley: We recently changed fallback order to prefer client_ip when cookie parse failed to reduce cross-device stickiness.
Kevin: That change introduced an edge-case: client_ip hash path treats empty IP as 0; for some HTTP/2 multiplexed requests X-Forwarded-For is `-` so hash(0) -> bucket 0. Canary happened to own bucket 0-3276.
Priya: Can you paste a raw request log?
Jon: ```INFO route=api-prod req_id=0a1b2c cookie="rw-session=abc123" X-Forwarded-For="-" header.X-Canary="" chosen_bucket=0 route=canary-2026-03-20```
Maria: XFF `-` means our proxy forwarded empty value, so fallback used 0. Not great.
Kevin: Repro steps locally: `curl --http2 -H 'X-Canary:' -b 'rw-session=' https://edge.internal/api` -> always canary. I can repro in a container with same proxy binary.
Jon: Ops impact: some customers saw quota/token spike because traffic routing concentrated on canary. Dashboard shows token burn.
DeployBot: canary rollout canary-2026-03-20 created at 2026-03-20T16:05:00Z by @kevin (weight=5).
Jon: We should consider rolling canary weight to 0 until fixed.
Kevin: I'll set weight 0 now.
DeployBot: canary-2026-03-20 weight updated 5 -> 0 by @kevin at 2026-03-20T16:22:14Z.
Ashley: Longer-term: add telemetry 'routing.fallback_source' with values [cookie, header, ip, none] and histogram of chosen_bucket to detect low-entropy bias.
Priya: Also add unit/integration test: simulate missing/empty headers and assert distribution within ±2% of expected.
Kevin: Hotfix plan: 1) treat empty/`-` X-Forwarded-For as missing; 2) when no entropy available, use server-side deterministic PRNG seeded with req_id instead of 0; 3) add explicit guard to avoid mapping 0 -> reserved canary range. PR #4123 opened.
Jon: Can we patch prod quickly? How long to rollout?
Kevin: Patch ready, rolling to edge proxies now. ETA ~15m for full roll. Pushing canary to single node for verification.
Jon: Quick check logs from node-7 after patch: ```INFO node=node-7 route=api-prod req_id=99aa cookie="" X-Forwarded-For="-" fallback=prng chosen_bucket=15203 route=stable-2026-02-01``` Good sign.
Maria: I also created dashboard alert: routing.canary_spike if canary_rate > expected + 10% for 1m. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/route-inference
Priya: Filing incident for tracking: INC-2026-128. Assigning Priya, Kevin.
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2026-128 created. Priority: P2.
Kevin: Patch fully rolled. Verifying global distribution now.
Jon: Confirmed distribution back to expected 5/95 across regions :thumbsup:
Ashley: Thanks — follow-ups: add telemetry, rollout UI to surface fallback policy (cookie/header/ip), and integration test.
Priya: I'll own the postmortem if incident persists.
Maria: Closing thread once all monitoring alerts clear. Good catch everyone.
